rebuttal_response: The claimed round-1 resolutions are not sufficient. The exact-output and diagnostic-comparison edits are present in the legacy test file, but that suite now fails during collection because the implementation no longer exports its expected API. The parser finding remains unresolved in substance: the current implementation uses tomlkit and ruamel.yaml instead of the specifically required tomli, tomli_w, and PyYAML libraries.

findings.title: Current implementation uses different parsers than the mandated pinned parsers
findings.criterion_ref: Criteria 1 and 8 require tomli==2.4.1, tomli_w==1.2.0, and PyYAML==6.0.3, including import-time exact-version enforcement.
findings.trigger: The structured codemod module is loaded or used for TOML or YAML processing.
findings.consequence: The mandated parser implementations and version-stability contract are absent, so the artifact cannot satisfy Criteria 1 or 8 regardless of whether its alternative libraries work.
findings.evidence: tools/refactor_repo/rewrite_structured_references.py imports `tomlkit` and `ruamel.yaml`, pins tomlkit==0.15.1 and ruamel.yaml==0.19.1, and contains no tomli, tomli_w, PyYAML safe_load, or PyYAML dump implementation. This contradicts the v2 report’s claimed three-parser fix.

findings.title: Required fixture suite fails during test collection
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 2 requires all fixtures to pass transformation testing with exact output or diagnostics.
findings.consequence: No fixture, determinism, idempotence, unsafe-input, or dry-run test executes, so the required passing test matrix does not exist for the delivered implementation.
findings.evidence: Pytest stops during collection with `ImportError: cannot import name 'DiagnosticKind'`. The test imports DiagnosticKind, DiagnosticSeverity, StructuredTransformation, TransformationResult, transform_file, and transform_files_dry_run, while the current implementation exports a different RewriteResult/rewrite_text API. The report’s claim of 21/21 passing is therefore false for the artifact on disk.

findings.title: Implementation does not support key-path-scoped transformations
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 7 requires transformations to apply only when both file format and key path match.
findings.trigger: A document contains the old substring in multiple string values, including values outside the intended target key path.
findings.consequence: The walker rewrites every matching string scalar, including unrelated paths, so transformations can cross their authorized key-path boundary.
findings.evidence: The current API accepts a global `mapping: dict[str, str]`; `_toml_walk`, `_yaml_walk`, and `_json_walk` traverse all values, and each leaf replacement applies substring replacement without checking a StructuredTransformation key_path. The prior key-path-aware StructuredTransformation API is absent.

observations: The legacy fixture test now uses direct content equality, and its determinism test compares diagnostic fields after checking equal list lengths; those two round-1 test assertions were edited as claimed.

The v2 report describes the implementation as unchanged from v1 and based on tomli/tomli_w/PyYAML, but the implementation on disk is a different tomlkit/ruamel.yaml codemod with a different public API.
Malformed-YAML coverage remains absent from the referenced legacy fixture suite.
reasoning: I compared the round history with my own prior verdict, inspected the v2 report and current implementation, and executed the cited pytest suite. The history is accurate, but the report does not describe the code currently on disk. The wrong parser stack, non-collecting tests, and absence of key-path scoping each directly defeat explicit acceptance criteria and survive the blocker-only threshold.
